body:

[Fake Account] Can’t see the mention of the upper spending cap any more in the Ts&Cs
[team teri] That gets you a Breville Barista Express for $449
Or, for those who want to pair the same extraction with a better grinder, the Infuser for $280 .
[mouzii] I'm looking to buy my first coffee machine, which of these is more user friendly?
[team teri] Neither ;-) They are pretty much identical when it comes to making coffee. One has an inbuilt grinder, the other doesn't.
Not sure if "user friendly" is the question you actually meant to ask. Easier for beginners would be the Bambino Plus . It can automatically steam milk for you. Also an exceptionally good price of $350 after cashback here.
I personally find the Bambino less user friendly, since I am competent at steaming milk manually, and very much would miss the pressure gauge that comes with the other two.
[fLaMePrO] Infuser was my first machine, still going strong 6 years later. Recommend it with the Smart Grinder Pro if you can find a deal on that too. $280 is a bloody good deal, I paid $450 back in COVID times but it has shot up since then.
If you're willing to learn, it will serve you well for years to come. Just invest in a few extras like a distributor, scale, better tamper and you are set.
I am currently on Aldi beans, I was spending $40-50 per kg but honestly the value proposition of Aldi medium roast for $18 is just really hard to beat. Will still buy some other beans occasionally, you have to spend some time dialling them in so allow some patience but it's a fun journey and once you pick it up, it makes it much harder to enjoy coffee away from home :P
